q: Before a trailer can be used on the road, what does it need?
choices: Only the towing vehicle's registration
Valid Alberta registration and a rear licence plate
A licence plate on the front only
Nothing, if it weighs under 910 kg
hint: Think about what the guide says every trailer needs before it goes on the road, no matter its weight.
explain: A trailer needs valid Alberta registration, carried with you while towing, and a valid licence plate on the rear that is clearly visible. Both are required before it can be used on the road.
quote: There must also be a valid licenCe plate attached to the rear of the trailer and clearly visible. The registration and licence plate are required before the trailer can be used on the road.

q: When you tow a trailer, where must the trailer's registration be?
choices: With you while you are towing it
At home with your other papers
On file at the registry only
With the trailer's owner only
hint: Think about what a peace officer might ask to see at the roadside.
explain: You must have valid Alberta registration for your trailer, and it must be with you when you are towing it.
quote: You must have valid registration from an Alberta registry for your trailer and it must be with you when you are towing the trailer.

q: Which lights must a trailer have?
choices: Only reflectors, since the towing vehicle has lights
Tail-lights only, since brake lights are optional
Turn signals only, switched on at the trailer
Tail-lights, brake lights and turn signals worked from the towing vehicle
hint: The trailer can hide your vehicle's own lights from drivers behind you.
explain: A trailer must have working tail-lights, brake lights and turn signals that are activated from the towing vehicle.
quote: Your trailer must have working tail-lights, brake lights, and turn signals that are activated from the towing vehicle.

q: Your trailer uses a ball-and-socket hitch. How should the safety chains be attached?
choices: Run straight back, one on each side, not crossed
Left loose on top of the hitch for quick removal
Crossed under the trailer's tongue and fastened securely
Chains are not needed with a ball-and-socket hitch
hint: Think about how the chains are arranged beneath the front of the trailer.
explain: With a ball-and-socket hitch you need safety chains between the trailer and towing vehicle, crossed under the trailer's tongue and fastened securely. This applies to all trailers except fifth-wheel trailers.
quote: If you have a ball-and-socket hitch, you will also need to attach safety chains between the trailer and the towing vehicle. Chains should be crossed under the tongue of the trailer and fastened securely.

q: When must you use extension mirrors while towing a trailer?
choices: Only when towing at night
When the trailer is wider than the towing vehicle
Only on multi-lane highways
When the trailer is shorter than the towing vehicle
hint: Think about what could block your view of traffic coming from behind.
explain: You must use extension mirrors if the trailer is wider than the vehicle towing it, so you can clearly see traffic approaching from behind.
quote: You must use extension mirrors if the trailer is wider than the vehicle that is towing the trailer.

q: The guide says a trailer with a gross weight at or below a certain amount does not require brakes. What is that amount?
choices: 910 kilograms
500 kilograms
1,500 kilograms
2,000 kilograms
hint: The number in kilograms is less than 1,000.
explain: Trailers with a gross weight of 910 kg (2,000 lb) or less do not require brakes. Watch the units: 2,000 is the weight in pounds, not kilograms.
quote: the following trailers do not require brakes: - trailers with a gross weight of 910 kilograms (2,000 pounds) or less

q: You are towing a trailer on a multi-lane highway and moving slower than other traffic. Which lane should you use?
choices: The left lane
The centre lane
Whichever lane is emptiest
The right lane
hint: Slower vehicles keep to one side so faster traffic can pass.
explain: On a multi-lane highway, slower-moving vehicles should travel in the right lane.
quote: If you are driving on a multi-lane highway, remember that slower-moving vehicles should travel in the right lane.
topic: Lane position and lane choice (right lane for slower traffic)

q: You are towing a trailer and a line of traffic builds up behind you. What should you do?
choices: Stop in your lane so they can go around you
Turn on your hazard lights and keep driving
Find a safe place off the road to stop and let them pass
Keep going, since it is their job to wait
hint: Think about how to let faster drivers get by safely.
explain: If traffic builds behind you, find a safe place to stop off the road to allow others to pass.
quote: If traffic builds behind you, find a safe place to stop off the road to allow others to pass.
topic: Towing trailers (driving with added weight and length)

q: What is off-tracking when you are towing a trailer?
choices: The trailer wheels follow a path outside your vehicle's wheels in a turn
The trailer wheels follow a path inside your vehicle's wheels in a turn
The trailer sways from side to side at highway speed
The trailer pushes your vehicle forward when you brake
hint: Watch the trailer wheels in your mirror during a turn.
explain: During a turn, the trailer wheels travel a path inside the path of your vehicle's wheels. This is called off-tracking.
quote: The trailer wheels will travel a path that is inside the path of the wheels of your vehicle. This is called off-tracking.

q: While towing a trailer, you make a right turn without allowing for off-tracking. What could happen?
choices: The trailer could hit a curb, a parked vehicle or a pedestrian
The trailer could swing wide into the oncoming lane
The trailer wheels could ride over the centre line
Nothing, since a trailer follows your exact path
hint: Remember which way the trailer wheels cut during a turn.
explain: In a turn the trailer wheels track inside your vehicle's wheels. On a right turn, if you do not allow for this, you could make contact with a curb, a parked vehicle or a pedestrian.
quote: To turn right, reverse these directions. However, if you do not allow for the off-tracking you could make contact with a curb, a parked vehicle, or a pedestrian.

q: You are backing up with a trailer and want the trailer to go left. Which way do you begin turning the steering wheel?
choices: To the left
Keep it straight and let the trailer drift
Turn it fully one way, then the other
To the right
hint: Backing a trailer works opposite to backing a vehicle on its own.
explain: Begin backing by turning the steering wheel in the opposite direction you want to go. Turn it right to send the trailer left, and use only small steering movements.
quote: Begin backing by turning the steering wheel in the opposite direction you want to go. Turn the steering wheel right to go left.

q: How fast should you reverse when backing a trailer?
choices: No faster than 20 km/h
The same speed as backing with no trailer
No faster than a walking pace
Fast enough to finish before traffic arrives
hint: Backing a trailer takes practice, so give yourself time to react.
explain: Always reverse no faster than a walking pace. Have someone guide you, or walk to the back of the trailer first to make sure the path is clear.
quote: Always reverse no faster than a walking pace.
